paper_metadata.title: In-situ formation of Ni3Ta nanophase for strengthening tungsten alloy

evidence.quote: a nano-Ni3Ta phase-reinforced ultrafine-grain tungsten alloy was fabricated via low-temperature sintering

This paper investigated the effects of adding Ta (0, 5, 10, and 15 wt. %) on the sintering behavior, microstructure, and mechanical properties of the alloy. For the first time, densification sintering of a W-Ta-Ni-Fe-Cu system was achieved via vacuum sintering at 1350 °C.

When the Ta content was increased to 15 wt. %, a considerable amount of Ni was consumed. This changed the ratio between Ni and Fe and resulted in the disappearance of the γ-(Ni,Fe) phase and the appearance of the Fe7W6 phase.
The morphology of the Cu-rich phase is nearly spherical, with a diameter of 30–70 nm, and there is apparent repulsion between Cu and both Fe and Ni.

attributes.morphology: two-phase structure with tungsten particles uniformly dispersed in the matrix

evidence.quote: the W-NF3C alloy exhibits a two-phase structure with tungsten particles (indicated by the green arrow) and a matrix phase (indicated by the red arrow). Tungsten particles were uniformly dispersed in the black matrix phase, and apparent diffusion was observed at the interface.

When 5 wt. % Ta was added, a small amount of dark gray Ta oxide (indicated by the white arrow) was scattered near the phase boundary, and the tungsten particles were refined. Also, a fine and distributed gray acicular phase (indicated by the yellow arrow) are seen in the matrix phase.

attributes.morphology: combined growth, distributed in a grid shape

evidence.quote: In the W-10Ta-NF3C alloy, a substantial amount of Ta oxide formed. The acicular phase has combined growth in the lath phase (indicated by the blue arrow), and the growth is distributed in a grid shape.
